text: The 2014 North Miami mayoral special election occurred on November 4, 2014, after a primary held on August 26, 2014. Following her 2013 election victory, Mayor Lucie Tondreau was indicted by federal prosecutors on charges involving an $8 million mortgage fraud scheme. She was subsequently suspended from office by Governor Rick Scott, leading to the special election to fill the remainder of her term. Three candidates participated in the special election: former Mayor Kevin Burns, former City Councilman Jean Marcellus, and physician Smith Joseph, all of whom had previously failed to win in the prior mayoral election. In the primary, Burns received 45 percent of the vote and placed first, advancing to a runoff against Joseph, who earned 38 percent and placed second. Joseph won the runoff with 54 percent to Burns’ 46 percent and served out the remainder of Tondreau’s term. Philippe Bien-Aime and Smith Joseph are both listed as nonpartisan.
